title: weave findings
description: weave-patch-schema v1 — the READ side of weave's agent contract. What a merge did, what it might have broken, and what the caller could do about it. The finding classes below are the fixed set of class tags a finding can carry. The WRITE side (`weave patch`) is a separate schema: schema/weave-ops.schema.json.

schema_version.description: Semver of THIS schema. Consumers must reject a major they do not know. Additive fields are minor bumps; removing or re-meaning a field is a major bump. 1.1.0 added the optional `scope` and `findings[].side`. 1.2.0 added `findings[].hunks`, `findings[].refused_by` and `findings[].texts`: a CONFLICT finding now DIAGNOSES the disagreement (which lines of base each side rewrote, where those rewrites meet, and which refusal fired) and REFERENCES the three full texts by `path@rev` instead of carrying them. `base`/`ours`/`theirs` remain valid and were always optional, so a 1.2.0 document is readable by a 1.1.0 consumer; a consumer that DEPENDED on the texts being inlined should read `texts[*].path@rev` and fetch them, which costs one `git show` and is why the worst-case document for a large conflicted file fell from 450KB to under 30KB. 1.3.0 added the advisory register: a new `source` value `advisory`, a new `finding_class` value `COOCCUPANCY`, the `warning_kind` value `sibling_co_change`, and the optional `findings[].cochange` object. An advisory reports a derivable fact about a CLEAN merge — a container both sides changed different siblings of — and never a risk or a refusal, so it changes no verdict and no exit code; a 1.2.0 consumer that does not know the new `source`/`class` values should treat the finding as informational rather than rejecting the document. A producer declares the lowest version whose fields it actually uses. Only additive changes, so a 1.3.0 document remains readable by a 1.x consumer.

file.description: Repository-relative path of the merged file. For scope=repo this is the file the finding is ABOUT — the one still carrying the broken use, not the one that broke it (that file appears in `related[].file`).

scope.description: What this document describes. `merge` (default when absent): one merge of one file, produced by the merge driver's read side. `repo`: a repo-scope binding check (`weave check`), which composes no text and therefore reports no ops — the cross-file half of the binding check, which a per-file driver structurally cannot see. Added in 1.1.0.

clean.description: True when the merge produced no conflict markers. NOTE: clean is not the same as safe — a clean merge can still carry findings (that is the entire point of this schema).

confidence.description: weave's own confidence in the resolution, coarse and monotone.

findings.description: Everything the caller should look at, in the finite class vocabulary. Empty means weave found nothing — NOT that nothing is wrong (the semantic layer is undecidable and is CI's job).

ops.description: Per-entity composition record: what happened to each entity key in this merge.

stats.description: Raw per-merge counters. Advisory; shape may grow.

finding_class.description: The class tags a finding can carry: DANGLING, DUP, SHADOW and ORDER for name-resolution changes, plus INTERLEAVE for effectful order composition, LOSS for content that no side dropped, ASYM for direction-dependent results, CONFLICT for the honest refusal, and COOCCUPANCY (1.3.0) for the advisory that a clean container merge composed different siblings from each side.

op_vocabulary.description: The per-entity actions. The first seven are the per-key actions a per-key matcher can emit on its own. The last four are the relational extension: they correlate several keys, which a per-key matcher cannot do. They are RESERVED — a v1 producer never emits split/merged/copied/moved; a v1 consumer must accept them without error.

side.description: Which version of the merge triple a fact came from.

cochange.description: The members each side changed or added in a clean container merge. Added in 1.3.0.

cochange_member.description: One member one side changed or added.

change.description: What this side did to the member.

entity.description: Entity key the finding is about. `(file)` when the finding is about the file as a whole.

entity_type.description: Parser-reported kind: function, class, method, interface, file, …

source.description: Where the finding came from. `conflict`: weave refused to guess. `warning`: weave resolved but flagged semantic risk. `derived`: computed from the merge output plus binding facts (renames/deletes) — the read-only form of the binding pass. `advisory` (1.3.0): weave resolved cleanly and reports a fact, not a risk — the lowest register, never blocking. A clean merge with only `advisory` findings is still clean.

side.description: Which side's change caused the finding — the actor, not the victim. For a repo-scope DANGLING this is the side that renamed or deleted the definition. Added in 1.1.0.

complexity.description: Conflict complexity classification — which dimensions of the entity changed.

confidence.description: How confident weave is that an automatic resolution would be right.

base.description: Entity content in the merge base. Null when absent there. Since 1.2.0 the merge producer does not emit this: `texts` says where the content is and `hunks` says what changed in it. Still valid, still optional.

ours.description: Entity content on our side. Null when absent there. Since 1.2.0 the merge producer does not emit this: `texts` says where the content is and `hunks` says what changed in it. Still valid, still optional.

theirs.description: Entity content on their side. Null when absent there. Since 1.2.0 the merge producer does not emit this: `texts` says where the content is and `hunks` says what changed in it. Still valid, still optional.

suggestion.description: A concrete next action, in the imperative. Advisory — never a resolution weave applied.

warning_kind.description: Present when source=warning: the underlying weave-core WarningKind, kept because the class mapping is lossy. `composition_licensed` is not a risk at all — it is a conflict weave RESOLVED under disjoint composition, carrying the two read/write sets that licensed it. `conflict_frame_duplicate` reports a line the frame of a conflicted output states more often than any union of the two sides could; it is the DUP class, found outside the markers, where no resolution removes it (added 1.2.0).

cochange.description: Present when class=COOCCUPANCY (source=advisory): the members each side changed or added in a container that merged clean. The two member lists never share a member — a member both sides touched is a conflict or an identical edit, not co-occupancy. Added in 1.3.0.

related.description: Other entities implicated in this finding.

hunks.description: The three-way alignment of this conflict, one entry per place the two sides' edits meet. Every field is READ OFF the two base-relative diffs weave already computed — nothing here is inferred and nothing is guessed. A finding without this reads as nearly useless to an agent trying to resolve the conflict — there is no per-hunk detail to act on. Added in 1.2.0.

refused_by.description: WHICH refusal fired. `kind` is the verdict (the two sides disagreed); this is the reason. The rungs are not interchangeable: `statement_fold` means diff3, the decorator merge and the container merge all passed and two edits landed in one statement, while `merge_ladder_exhausted` means every rung refused. Added in 1.2.0.

texts.description: Where the three full texts are, rather than the three full texts. Added in 1.2.0.

from.description: Previous name. Present for op=renamed / rename_edited.

to.description: New name. Present for op=renamed / rename_edited.

conflicted.description: True when this op describes the SHAPE of a conflict rather than an applied resolution. The entity also appears in `findings` with class=CONFLICT.

fallback.description: True when weave could not use entity-level merging here and fell back to line-level merge. The op is then a best-effort description.

bindings.description: The facts a caller needs to check name resolution itself — the inputs to the DANGLING / DUP / SHADOW classes.

renames.description: Every rename weave observed, with the side that performed it. A caller repairing call sites needs exactly this.

references.description: Per entity key touched by this merge: is it still defined in the merged output, and is it still referenced there? `referenced && !defined` is precisely the DANGLING condition, and is reported as a derived finding.

base_start.description: First base line this hunk replaces, 1-based and inclusive, counted INSIDE the entity's own base text (the one `texts.base` references) — not inside the file. A finding is about an entity, and a range stated against anything else would need a second coordinate system to be checkable.

base_end.description: Last base line this hunk replaces, inclusive. `base_end < base_start` is a pure INSERTION before `base_start`: an insertion has a position, not an extent.

collision.description: The base lines BOTH sides rewrote or deleted — the lines two developers each had an opinion about, which is the question the marker is asking. Absent or empty means the two edits are merely ADJACENT: one hunk because nothing separates them, not because they contradict.

action.description: What this side did to this hunk. `untouched` means only the OTHER side touched it.

removed.description: Base lines this side deleted, verbatim and in order.

added.description: Lines this side wrote in their place, verbatim and in order.

tokens_added.description: Identifiers present in what this side wrote and absent from what it deleted — a set difference over tokens. It names what APPEARED. It does not claim to know why, because a merge tool that summarises intent is guessing.

tokens_removed.description: Identifiers present in what this side deleted and absent from what it wrote.

path.description: Repository-relative path the text lives in.

rev.description: The revision to read it at: `git show <rev>:<path>`. Absent when the producer genuinely does not know one — the merge driver is handed three temp files by git and a `rev` it invented would be worse than none.

lines.description: How many lines the entity's text has there, so a reader can budget the fetch.

content_hash.description: A 16-hex-digit fingerprint of the entity's text, for answering “is this still the version the finding was computed against”. A fingerprint, NOT a cryptographic commitment: it is Rust's `DefaultHasher`, and the schema says so rather than letting the field name imply otherwise.
